intuition: Save each value in a set as you read the array. If a value is already there, an earlier position contained the same value, so a duplicate exists. This replaces comparing each number with every other number.

A set retains the distinct values already encountered. Before inserting the next value, ask whether it is present. Presence means an earlier occurrence exists, so the current index completes a duplicate pair. Absence means this is its first appearance and it should be remembered.

The set intentionally ignores occurrence positions and exact frequencies because neither affects the answer. Early return avoids scanning the rest after a duplicate is proved. If the scan completes, every insertion was a first occurrence, which proves that all elements are distinct. Hash lookup gives expected linear total time.

steps: For nums=[1,2,3,1], begin with seen=set() as an empty set.
At index 0, value 1 is absent. Insert it, giving seen={1}.
At index 1, value 2 is absent. Insert it, giving seen={1,2}.
At index 2, value 3 is absent. Insert it, giving seen={1,2,3}.
At index 3, value 1 is already in the set. Its earlier occurrence was at index 0.
Return true immediately. The answer depends on repeated value 1, not on whether the duplicate positions are adjacent.

concept.observation: Check earlier membership before adding the current occurrence.
approach: Begin with an empty set of earlier values.
For each value, return yes if it is already present.
Otherwise add it; return no if the full scan finds no repeat.
concept.correctness: The set contains exactly the values processed earlier. Membership for the current value therefore holds exactly when an earlier equal occurrence exists. A successful test witnesses two distinct positions; if every test fails, all input occurrences are distinct.

complexity.explanation: Each value receives one expected-constant-time membership test and insertion. Work is expected linear, with up to linear set storage.

pitfalls: Check earlier membership before adding the current occurrence.
